justification: Assessment returned INVALID but targets a different defect than the ground truth. Ground truth: Theorem 1 (Inversion Formula, lines 0165-0183) omits the essential hypothesis alpha(1) != 0 (beta(1) = 1/alpha(1)); witness alpha == 0, G(1)=1, X=1. The assessment explicitly listed that theorem as checked_ok (verified 'with general alpha(1) = a', i.e. tacitly assuming a != 0) and never raised the nonvanishing hypothesis. Its primary claim is an unproved black box at lines 0551-0559; its concrete counterexample is a distinct n=1 defect in the SPECIALIZED formula at lines 0216-0219. I verified that concrete defect directly against the source: with alpha(n,y)=1 iff P^-(n)>y and P^-(1)=infinity, alpha(1,y)=1, so Theorem 1 forces beta(1,y)=1/alpha(1,y)=1; but the displayed beta(n,y)=sum_{k=1}^{Omega(n)}(-1)^k d_k^*(n,y) is an empty sum at n=1 (Omega(1)=0), giving beta(1,y)=0. Taking 1 <= X < 2, identity (5) at line 0214 reads M(X,y) = beta(floor(X/2)+1,y) = beta(1,y) = 0, while M(1,y) = mu(1) = 1 by the definition at line 0159 (P^-(1)=infinity>y). So (5) asserts 1 = 0. I also confirmed the propagated failure of the recursion at line 0227: d_2'(1,y)=1, d_1^*(1,y)=d_1'(1,y)=1, and d_2^*(1,y)=0 (empty constrained sum), so the recursion reads 0 = 1 - 2 = -1. The flaw is genuine and independently checked, but it is not the ground-truth defect, hence CAUGHT_DIFFERENT rather than CAUGHT_MATCHING or FALSE_CATCH.
